newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF'S RECORD RUN COMES TO AN END.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF'S RECORD RUN COMES TO AN END.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf's defeat in the Australian Open on Sunday ended the longest match-winning run in professional grand slam history.

Twelfth-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer stunned the centre court crowd by producing the best performance of her 10-year career to beat the German top seed 6-2 7-5 on a scorching day at Melbourne Park.
It was Graf's worst result in Melbourne since she lost in the third round as a 14-year-old in 1984 and ended a run of 45 match victories in tennis's four major events.
Graf's extraordinary record in the professional era dates back to her defeat in the U.S. Open final in 1994 when she lost to Spain's Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.

The German, who had long bettered Margaret Smith Court's record of 35 consecutive grand slam victories, wilted in heat said to be up to 50 degrees Celsius on centre court, during a day of upsets in the women's tournament.
Graf, whose father Peter's trial on tax evasion charges is expected to reach a verdict on January 24, left the stadium immediately after the match suffering from heat exhaustion.
A WTA statement said Graf was also suffering from an infected toe.
"Hot temperatures during today's match exacerbated her condition resulting in heat illness," the statement said. Graf had returned to her hotel and was in a stable condition.

In the same statement, Graf paid tribute to her opponent. "She played really well today. I tried everything I could, I tried as hard as I could. I just didn't have the energy with the heat. But give her credit, she handled the conditions really well."
Graf's stunning exit followed fourth round losses by third seed Conchita Martinez of Spain, German fifth seed Anke Huber and seventh seed Lindsay Davenport.
Coetzer played the match of her life, taking the first set in 27 minutes and recovering from a 4-0 deficit to clinch the tie in 88 minutes.
Graf started to receive medical treatment midway through the second set as both players struggled in the oppressive conditions.
Coetzer said the victory was the best of her career, adding: "You often tend to see the top players come out of tight situations at Grand Slams, so this is very important for me."
In the opening set Graf consistently speared her usually reliable backhand into the net and sprayed her fierce forehands long and wide.
"I felt comfortable playing to her forehand, she was definitely making a lot of errors," said Coetzer.
Graf appeared to regain her composure at the start of the second set but withered in the burning sun, allowing Coetzer to book a quarter-final berth against American Kimberly Po.
Coetzer, a semifinalist in the Open last year, was rewarded for her valiant baseline play as she doggedly chased down everything her opponent could offer.
Graf netted a succession of simple smash volleys and dropped her last service game with a double-fault, allowing Coetzer to serve for the match.
